newsitem.title: FRANCE: FIGURE SKATING-RUSSIAN TITLE SWEEP LOOMS LARGE.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-RUSSIAN TITLE SWEEP LOOMS LARGE.

text.p: The late addition of Olympic and
world ice dance champions Oksana Gritschuk and Evgeny Platov to
the team has enhanced the chances of a Russian title sweep at
next week's European figure skating championships.
Even with last year's pairs champions Artur Dmitriev and
Oksana Kazakova on the sidelines, Russian power and depth
through all four events could produce an unprecedented
domination of the gold medals.
Gritschuk and Platov were listed only as substitutes
following the recent national championships in hopes that they
would get back into top form for the world championships in
Lausanne in March.
But Russian officials confirmed on Wednesday that the
champions, who have left former coach Natalia Linichuk to join
the renowned Tatiana Tarasova, would defend their title at the
Europeans at Bercy in Paris next week.
Even without the late change of heart, Russia would have
been favoured for gold through Anjelika Krylova and Oleg
Ovsiannikov, second at last year's European and world events and
natural successors to the title.
France should have a say in the final distribution of the
dance medals with two strong couples, the fast improving Marina
Anissina and Gwendal Peizerat and the former medallists Sophie
Moniotte and Pascal Lavanchy, second two years ago before injury
forced them out of action last season.
Russia's Dmitriev achieved a welcome if slightly unexpected
victory with new partner Kazakova in Sofia a year ago, four
years after he and former partner Natalia Mishkutienok had
captured Olympic gold in Albertville.
But the new pair could only finish fourth in the recent
Russian national championships and so with only three couples
from their country permitted next week they were ordered to sit
and wait to see if they could break into the team for Lausanne.
Yet such is the strength of Russian pairs skating that they
may not be missed. Erratic former champions Marina Eltsova and
Andrei Bushkov, fourth a year ago before they went on to capture
the world title, were consistent and spectacular in winning the
national title as two other former champions, Evgenia Shishkova
and Vadim Naumov, placed third.
But if the Russians are vulnerable, it is in this event
where Germans Mandy Wotzel and Ingo Steuer, the 1995 champions,
could again displace them.
Officials have once again changed the qualification rules in
the singles events this season and all the entrants in the men's
and women's singles will have to qualify on Sunday and Monday
for the final fields of 24.
Russians Alexei Urmanov, the Olympic champion, and 1995
European champion Ilya Kulik have had fine seasons and either
one could depose reigning champion Viacheslav Zagorodniuk next
week.
The Russians have a third string to their bow in 16-year-old
leaper Alexei Yagudin, who threatens to eclipse them all in
future years. Zagorodniuk could struggle to get a medal.
Russia's silver medallist last year, Igor Pashkevich, will
skate under the Azerbaijan banner after being upset because he
was dropped from the Russian team for last year's worlds in
Canada despite being second in Sofia.
Teenager Irina Slutskaya made a major breakthrough for the
team a year ago when she became the first Russian woman to win
an international championship title. She then placed third in
the world championship.
She was third in the national championships last month
behind Maria Butyrskaya and Olga Markova, either one of whom
could beat her again.
Two potential rivals to the Russians are both substitutes,
including five-times champion Surya Bonaly of France. She was
left off the team despite winning her national title because
officials decided her form was still not good enough after a
lengthy period out with injury last year.
German Tanja Szewczenko, the famous other half of the
high-speed Olympic crash with Oksana Baiul in Lillehammer in
1994, has recovered from a mystery virus but missed all her
pre-season training and is not yet ready for competition.
